title: SkillSpec: Consensus-Gated Agent Skill Evolution via Representation Specialization
abstract: arXiv:2610.00704v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Natural-language skills are textual procedural memories through which large language model (LLM) agents retain reusable task knowledge without updating model weights. Existing methods typically treat skills as either static artifacts or monolithic documents optimized using aggregate validation scores as feedback. However, representing a skill as a monolithic document restricts optimization to its textual content, without explicitly modeling the structure through which procedural knowledge is retrieved and executed. We identify a key distinction between learning what knowledge to retain and determining how to organize it: textual updates should first be validated through execution evidence, after which the retained knowledge should be structured according to its procedural dependencies and retrieval requirements. translated_title: SkillSpec：通过表示特化实现基于共识门控的智能体技能演化
translated_abstract: 自然语言技能是文本形式的程序性记忆，大型语言模型（LLM）智能体借助它在不更新模型权重的情况下保留可复用的任务知识。现有方法通常将技能视为静态产物或单一整体文档，并使用聚合验证分数作为反馈进行优化。然而，将技能表示为单一整体文档会将优化限制在其文本内容上，而没有显式建模程序性知识被检索和执行时所依赖的结构。我们识别出一个关键区别：学习保留什么知识与决定如何组织知识是不同的——文本更新应首先通过执行证据加以验证，之后保留的知识应根据其程序性依赖关系和检索需求进行结构化组织。为此，我们提出了SkillSpec，一个包含共识门控演化和表示特化两个阶段的框架。
tldr: SkillSpec提出两阶段框架，先通过执行证据对技能文本更新进行共识门控验证，再依据程序性依赖和检索需求对保留知识进行表示特化，从而优化LLM智能体的自然语言技能组织与演化。
en_tdlr: SkillSpec is a two-phase framework that first validates skill text updates through consensus-gated execution evidence, then specializes the retained knowledge's representation according to procedural dependencies and retrieval requirements to optimize LLM agent skills.
